units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:7:1">Y. Ber. VI, end, 10ᵈ</cite> <he>על כל … שהיה פוֹתֵהַ וכ׳</he> over each cask as he opened it he said the benediction &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 104a:6">Sabb. 104ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>פּוֹתְחִין לו</he> (Var. <he>פְּתָחִין</he>), v. <cite ref="I00529"><he>טָמֵא</he> I</cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 48a:9">Ib. 48ᵃ</cite> <he>מתירין … אבל לא פותחין</he> you may untie the neck-hole of a shirt, but not cut it open (on the Sabbath).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 1:3:6">Y. Taan. I, 64ᵇ</cite> top (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 45:8">Is. XLV, 8</cite>) <he>כנקבה … פוֹתַחַת וכ׳</he> like the female that opens for the male.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 3:4">Ned. III, 4</cite> <he>לא יִפְתַּח לו בנדר</he> he must not begin (offer his willingness) to make a vow (in order to escape robbery &c., v. <cite ref="N00239"><he>נָדַר</he></cite>); a. v. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="Q02132"><he>פָּתוּחַ</he></cite>; <he>פְּתוּחָה</he>; pl. <he>פְּתוּחִים</he>, <he>פְּתוּחִין</he>; <he>פְּתוּחוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Yevamot 71b">Yeb. 71ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>נסתם הפ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="O01705"><he>סָתַם</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 94a:6">Snh. 94ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="O01705"><he>סָתַם</he></cite> (v. <cite ref="M01810"><he>מנצפ״ך</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Megillah 3a:2">Meg. 3ᵃ</cite>, <he>פ׳ באמצע</he>, v. <cite ref="O01705"><he>סָתַם</he></cite>.

Erub. IV, 6 שלש חצירות הפ׳ זו לזו ופ׳ וכ׳ three courts opening into (communicating with) one another and into the publicroad; a. v. fr.—פתח פתוח, v. פֶּתַח.—Esp. (פרשה) פְּתוּחָה a paragraph in the Torah beginning with a new, indented line, opp. סתומה.

Treat. Sof’rim I, 14 איזהו פ׳ כל שלא וכ׳ what is an open paragraph? Such as does not begin at the beginning of a line, וכמה … ותהא נקראת פ׳ and how much space must one leave … for a paragraph to be called open?; a. fr.—Trnsf. [to open the door to,] to introduce (into learning).

Y. M. Kat. III, 83ᵇ top איזהו רבו כל שפ׳ לו תחלה who is called one’s (special) teacher? He who was the first to initiate him; a. e.—Esp. to open an opportunity for retracting a vow, to suggest reasons which, if known at the time, would have prevented the person from making the vow, v. חֲרָטָה.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 9:1">Ned. IX, 1</cite> <he>פותחין לאדם בכבוך וכ׳</he> the judges offer suggestions taken from the respect due to parents (saying, if you had known that this vow cast a reflection on your father &c.).

<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 9:1">Ib.</cite> <he>רִפְתְּחוּ לו בכבוד המקום</he> why not suggest to him the reverence due to the Lord (‘if you had known that he who makes a vow is considered an evil-doer &c.’)? Ib. 4 <he>פותחין לו מן הכתוב וכ׳</he> we offer suggestions to him from what is written in the Law, saying to him, if you had known that (in fulfilling that vow) you would transgress the law forbidding revenge &c.; a. fr.—
B. Kam. 27ᵃ פ׳ בכד וסיים בחבית the Mishnah begins with kad and closes with ḥabith! Ber. 10ᵃ פ׳ בה באשרי וכ׳, v. סוּם I h.

Gen. R. s. 84 אתה פָתַחְתָּ תחלה בהצלת וכ׳ thou wast the first man to speak of saving life; אתה פתחת בתשובה וכ׳ thou wast the first to do repentance, … one of thy descendants shall rise and be the first (prophet) to call for repentance; a. fr.—Esp. to open a lecture with a (Biblical) text. Pesik. Aḥăré, p. 170ᵃ ר׳ לוי פ׳ וכ׳ R. Levi took up the text (Ps. LXXV, 5) &c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 1:7">Gen. R. s. 1</cite>; a. v. fr.—
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 33:1">Pesik. R. s. 33</cite> [an editorial gloss] <he>פ׳ בכל אלו הפרשיות</he> the author takes his texts from all those (quoted) passages.

Shek. V, 1; Men. 65ᵃ (ref. to פתחיה as identical with מרדכי) he was named Pethahia, שהיה פותח דברים ודורשן וכ׳ (not בדברים) because he explained words and interpreted them (etymologically) and knew seventy languages.—Part. pass. as ab. Sifré Aḥăré, beg., v. סָתַם.
<cite ref="Yevamot 71b">Yeb. 71ᵇ</cite>, a. e., v. <cite ref="O01705"><he>סָתַם</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 16b:5-12">R. Hash. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>שלשה … נִפְתָּחִין בר״ה</he> three books are opened (for recording) on the New Year’s Day.

B. Bath. 125ᵇ, v. סוּם I, Nithpa. Pesik. R. l. c. להִיפָּתֵחַ to have one’s bowels opened, v. פְּסִיעָה; a. fr.—Ib. [editorial gloss] ונ׳ עוד שם בפרשת וכ׳ and furthermore this section (Is. LXI, 1) was used as the opening text; a. fr.—Esp. to have one’s eyes opened, to become seeing.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 42:1">Pesik. R. s. 42</cite> <he>כשילדה שדה כל סומא … נ׳</he> when Sarah gave birth, every blind person in the world was restored to sight; a. e.

senses.gloss: to open. Ib. פי׳ הפילקיות he opened the prisons.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Parah 3:8">Par. III, 8</cite> <he>ועושין … ומְפַתְּחִין בה חלונות</he> they piled wood in the shape of a tower and opened windows in it.

<cite ref="Zevachim 88b:2">Zeb. 88ᵇ</cite> <he>רימונים שלא פִיתְּחוּ פיהן</he> (Ms. K. a. R. 2 <he>נִפְתְּחוּ</he>; Ms. R. 1 <he>נִתְפַּתְּחוּ</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 5) pomegranates which have not yet burst open; a. e.

senses.gloss: to engrave. Y. Ab. Zar. III, 43ᵇ bot פי׳ בה פיתוחים if he cut designs into it.

units: <cite ref="Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 28">Pirké d’R. El. ch. XXVIII</cite>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 76">Gen. R. s. 76</cite> <he>כשיצמד … יְפַתְּחוּ וישדדו וכ׳</he> when an ox and a cow are harnessed together, they will break and harrow all valleys.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 31:1">Pesik. R. s. 31</cite> <he>נִתְפַּתְּחוּ בדם</he> they (their cavities) were opened with (discharged) blood; a. e.
